title: Big dataset — glove-100-angular (cosine, 1.2M)
subtitle: MyVector · vsql_vector · pgvector — 1.18M × 100-d word embeddings, cosine, published ground truth
nav: ← cross-engine (fashion-mnist) · MySQL versions · real-dataset · village
description: The big-dataset round: glove-100-angular — 1.18 million 100-d GloVe word embeddings with a cosine metric (vs the 60k×784 L2 fashion-mnist on the other pages). Recall@10 is scored against the dataset's published exact neighbors. GloVe is a genuinely hard ANN benchmark, so recall sits well below the ~0.99 of fashion-mnist — the interesting comparison is the recall/throughput tradeoff each engine strikes at this scale. Full metrics via MyVector's harness.
caveats: Dataset: glove-100-angular (ann-benchmarks) — 1.18M train × 100-d GloVe word vectors, 10k test, cosine. HNSW M=16, ef_construction=200. Recall is intrinsically lower than on fashion-mnist — GloVe is a hard, high-overlap embedding space.

Reading the sweep: MyVector tunes for throughput, so it reaches each recall at a lower ef_search — its per-point dots sit lower-and-righter, but at matched recall (the table above) it serves the most QPS across the mid-to-high recall range. MyVector's sweep is extended to ef_search=3200 (recall 0.985) to show it doesn't plateau — it goes higher than vsql (0.957) or pgvector (0.954) reached at ef=800; those two stop at ef=800 (their recall would also climb with more ef, but vsql's ~7 h rebuild made re-sweeping impractical).

Engine-isolated: each engine was benchmarked with the other engines stopped, so its 1.2M index build had the full A2 host (24 GB) to itself — building four 1.2M HNSW indexes with all servers resident OOMs the box. pgvector also needed --shm-size=4g for its parallel build.

Full metrics via MyVector's harness: build, insert QPS, exact brute-force KNN (QPS + p50/p99), ANN (QPS + p50/p99), recall@10 vs published ground truth. Headline cards are the warm ef_search=200 point.

Build time — super-linear, not a threading gap (verified): the same 1.2M HNSW index build took MyVector ~46 min and pgvector ~33 min but vsql_vector ~7 hours (the index build specifically; vsql's insert was ~3 min). We checked whether vsql was single-threaded — it isn't: its build runs ~4 threads (measured ~410% CPU, matching innodb_ddl_threads=4). The real cause is that vsql's build scales super-linearly: a 40k-row build takes ~100 s, but 1.18M took ~7 h — ~256× the time for ~30× the rows (≈ O(N^1.6)), far beyond the ~1 h a near-linear extrapolation predicts. So its graph construction degrades at scale (likely memory/cache-bound) while MyVector's and pgvector's stay efficient at 1.2M. Each engine used its default build path on the same 8-core host. MariaDB is excluded entirely — its online MHNSW build at 1.2M ran many hours without completing (it's on the fashion-mnist pages).
Hardware: Ampere A2 host (8 vCPU / 24 GB), one engine resident at a time.
